Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let

\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

First note that no \(a_n\) is \(0\). If \(a_n=0\) for some \(n>0\), then using the recurrence at index \(n-1\),

\[
a_{n-1}\equiv 0,
\]

and continuing down gives \(a_0=0\), impossible. Also \(a_n\not\equiv -1\pmod{397}\), since then the left side would be \(0\) while the right side would be \(-1\).

Thus from

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2\equiv a_n \pmod{397}
\]

we get

\[
a_{n+1}\equiv a_n(a_n+1)^{-2}\pmod{397},
\]

so

\[
b_{n+1}\equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
\equiv a_n+2+\frac1{a_n}
\equiv a_n+2+b_n \pmod{397}.
\]

Therefore

\[
a_n\equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2 \pmod{397}.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv \sum_{n=0}^{2026}(b_{n+1}-b_n)-2\cdot 2027
\equiv b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027 \pmod{397}.
\]

Since \(a_0=1\), we have \(b_0=1\). Also \(a_{2026}=9\), so

\[
b_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

Because \(397\equiv 1\pmod 9\), or directly \(9\cdot 353=3177\equiv 1\pmod{397}\),

\[
b_{2026}\equiv 353.
\]

Then

\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+2+a_{2026}
\equiv 353+2+9
\equiv 364\pmod{397}.
\]

Finally,

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-2\cdot 2027 \pmod{397}.
\]

Since

\[
2\cdot 2027=4054\equiv 84\pmod{397},
\]

we get

\[
364-1-84=279.
\]

Thus the required remainder is

\[
\boxed{279}.
\]
